subproblem.title: Hoelder bound for lower integrals of arbitrary [0,∞]-valued functions on a set
subproblem.statement: Let X be a type with a measurable-space structure, μ a measure on X, B ⊆ X an arbitrary subset, g : X → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed), and p, q real numbers with 0 < q ≤ p. Then, with Mathlib's lower Lebesgue integral ∫⁻_B f dμ := ∫⁻ f d(μ.restrict B) and real powers in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.rpow), ∫⁻_B g^q dμ ≤ (∫⁻_B g^p dμ)^{q/p} · μ(B)^{1-q/p}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (B : Set X) (g : X → ℝ≥0∞) (p q : ℝ), 0 < q → q ≤ p → ∫⁻ x in B, g x ^ q ∂μ ≤ (∫⁻ x in B, g x ^ p ∂μ) ^ (q / p) * μ B ^ (1 - q / p)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- ν := μ.restrict B. For every f : X → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_B f dμ is by definition ∫⁻ f dν.
- ∫⁻ 1 dν = μ(B) (setLIntegral_one).
- All powers of elements of [0, ∞] are ENNReal.rpow with real exponents.
- ∫⁻ is Mathlib's lower Lebesgue integral: the supremum of the integrals of measurable simple functions below the integrand. It is monotone in the integrand without any measurability assumption (lintegral_mono).

1. Exponents. Since 0 < q ≤ p:
   - p > 0 and p/q > 0;
   - a := q/p satisfies 0 < a ≤ 1 (div_pos, div_le_one);
   - b := 1 - q/p satisfies b ≥ 0, and a + b = 1;
   - (p/q)·(q/p) = 1 and q·(p/q) = p, because p ≠ 0 and q ≠ 0.

2. Measurable minorant. Apply exists_measurable_le_lintegral_eq to the measure ν and the function x ↦ g(x)^q. It gives a measurable G : X → [0, ∞] with G(x) ≤ g(x)^q for all x and ∫⁻ g^q dν = ∫⁻ G dν. Hence the left side of the claim equals ∫⁻ G dν.

3. Rewriting G. Put F(x) := G(x)^{p/q}.
   - F is measurable (Measurable.pow_const), hence AEMeasurable for ν. The constant function 1 is AEMeasurable.
   - For every x, F(x)^a · 1^b = (G(x)^{p/q})^{q/p} · 1 = G(x)^{(p/q)(q/p)} = G(x)^1 = G(x). This uses ENNReal.one_rpow, ENNReal.rpow_mul (x^{y z} = (x^y)^z), step 1 and ENNReal.rpow_one.

4. Hoelder. Apply ENNReal.lintegral_mul_norm_pow_le to the measure ν, f := F, g := 1 and the exponents a, b ≥ 0 with a + b = 1:
   ∫⁻ F^a · 1^b dν ≤ (∫⁻ F dν)^a · (∫⁻ 1 dν)^b.
   By step 3 and ∫⁻ 1 dν = μ(B), this reads
   ∫⁻ G dν ≤ (∫⁻ G^{p/q} dν)^{q/p} · μ(B)^{1-q/p}.
   - The lemma is the two-exponent form of Hoelder's inequality ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq with the conjugate exponents p/q and p/(p - q).
   - It handles the degenerate cases itself. If q = p, then b = 0 and μ(B)^0 = 1. The values 0 and ∞ of the integrals and of μ(B) are allowed.

5. Comparison with g^p.
   - For each x, G(x) ≤ g(x)^q and p/q ≥ 0. By ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow, G(x)^{p/q} ≤ (g(x)^q)^{p/q} = g(x)^{q·(p/q)} = g(x)^p (ENNReal.rpow_mul and step 1).
   - By monotonicity of the lower integral (lintegral_mono, no measurability needed), ∫⁻ G^{p/q} dν ≤ ∫⁻ g^p dν.
   - Since q/p ≥ 0, ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow gives (∫⁻ G^{p/q} dν)^{q/p} ≤ (∫⁻ g^p dν)^{q/p}.
   - Multiplying both sides by μ(B)^{1-q/p} keeps the inequality in [0, ∞] (monotonicity of multiplication).

6. Conclusion. Chain steps 2, 4 and 5:
   ∫⁻_B g^q dμ = ∫⁻ G dν
   ≤ (∫⁻ G^{p/q} dν)^{q/p} · μ(B)^{1-q/p}
   ≤ (∫⁻ g^p dν)^{q/p} · μ(B)^{1-q/p}
   = (∫⁻_B g^p dμ)^{q/p} · μ(B)^{1-q/p}. ∎
proof_key_steps: Exponents: p > 0, a = q/p ∈ (0,1], b = 1 - q/p ≥ 0, a + b = 1, (p/q)(q/p) = 1
exists_measurable_le_lintegral_eq on μ.restrict B gives measurable G ≤ g^q with ∫⁻_B g^q = ∫⁻_B G
ENNReal.lintegral_mul_norm_pow_le with f = G^{p/q}, g = 1: ∫⁻_B G ≤ (∫⁻_B G^{p/q})^{q/p} μ(B)^{1-q/p}
G^{p/q} ≤ (g^q)^{p/q} = g^p, then monotonicity of the lower integral and of x ↦ x^{q/p} and multiplication

audit.reason: The standalone one-line proposition matches every prose hypothesis, including arbitrary B and nonmeasurable g. The measurable minorant preserves the lower integral; the stated power identities, measurable Hölder application and monotonicity prove the exact bound. The proof covers q = p, zero mass and infinite values, requires no undeclared dependency, and is sufficiently detailed for formalization.

subproblem.title: Scaling inequality for the scaled L^p norm on nested closed balls
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} any subset, V a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) with weight μ := V.weight, and H : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ} any function. For p, r real and y a point let K(y, r) := V.scaledLpNorm H p y r = (ofReal(r^{p-n}) · ∫⁻_{B̄_r(y)} ‖H‖ₑ^p dμ)^{1/p} ∈ [0, ∞] (closed balls, lower integral, n read as a real number). If p > 0, 0 < s ≤ t and B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w), then K(z, s) ≤ ofReal((s/t)^{(p-n)/p}) · K(w, t).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p : ℝ) (z w : Amb n ℓ) (s t : ℝ), 0 < p → 0 < s → s ≤ t → closedBall z s ⊆ closedBall w t → V.scaledLpNorm H p z s ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((s / t) ^ ((p - n) / p)) * V.scaledLpNorm H p w t
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- μ := V.weight.
- I(y, r) := ∫⁻_{B̄_r(y)} ‖H‖ₑ^p dμ ∈ [0, ∞]: a lower integral, with H arbitrary.
- Unfolding RectifiableVarifold.scaledLpNorm gives K(y, r) = (ofReal(r^{p-n}) · I(y, r))^{1/p}.
- Real powers of nonnegative reals are Real.rpow; powers of elements of [0, ∞] are ENNReal.rpow. n stands for (n : ℝ).

1. Since 0 < s ≤ t, we have t > 0 and s/t > 0.

2. Monotonicity in the domain. B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w) gives I(z, s) ≤ I(w, t) (lintegral_mono_set; no measurability is needed).

3. Splitting the weight.
   - Real.div_rpow (s, t ≥ 0) gives (s/t)^{p-n} = s^{p-n} / t^{p-n}.
   - t^{p-n} > 0 (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos), so (s/t)^{p-n} · t^{p-n} = s^{p-n} (div_mul_cancel₀).
   - (s/t)^{p-n} ≥ 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg), so ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives ofReal(s^{p-n}) = ofReal((s/t)^{p-n}) · ofReal(t^{p-n}).

4. By step 3, associativity, step 2 and monotonicity of multiplication in [0, ∞]:
   ofReal(s^{p-n}) · I(z, s) = ofReal((s/t)^{p-n}) · (ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I(z, s))
   ≤ ofReal((s/t)^{p-n}) · (ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I(w, t)).

5. Taking 1/p-th powers. Since 1/p > 0, the map x ↦ x^{1/p} on [0, ∞] is monotone (ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow) and multiplicative (ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_nonneg). Hence
   K(z, s) = (ofReal(s^{p-n}) · I(z, s))^{1/p}
   ≤ (ofReal((s/t)^{p-n}) · (ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I(w, t)))^{1/p}
   = ofReal((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p} · (ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I(w, t))^{1/p}
   = ofReal((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p} · K(w, t).

6. The coefficient.
   - ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg ((s/t)^{p-n} ≥ 0 and 1/p ≥ 0) gives ofReal((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p} = ofReal(((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p}).
   - Real.rpow_mul (s/t ≥ 0) gives ((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p} = (s/t)^{(p-n)·(1/p)} = (s/t)^{(p-n)/p} (mul_one_div).
   Substituting into step 5 gives K(z, s) ≤ ofReal((s/t)^{(p-n)/p}) · K(w, t). Every step holds in [0, ∞], also when I(w, t) = ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: ofReal(s^{p-n}) = ofReal((s/t)^{p-n}) · ofReal(t^{p-n}) via Real.div_rpow and ENNReal.ofReal_mul
Take 1/p-th powers: monotone and multiplicative (ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow, ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_nonneg)
ofReal((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p} = ofReal((s/t)^{(p-n)/p}) via ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg and Real.rpow_mul

audit.reason: The standalone one-line type is exactly the parent's first conjunct and matches the prose. Positive radii justify the real-power factorization; domain monotonicity and nonnegative ENNReal powers yield the stated coefficient. Every step is valid for nonmeasurable H and infinite integrals. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and other children.

subproblem.title: Hoelder bound of the q-th power integral by the scaled L^p norm on a larger ball
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} any subset, V a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) with weight μ := V.weight, H : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ} any function, and K(y, r) := V.scaledLpNorm H p y r = (ofReal(r^{p-n}) · ∫⁻_{B̄_r(y)} ‖H‖ₑ^p dμ)^{1/p} ∈ [0, ∞] (closed balls, lower integrals). If 0 < q ≤ p, t > 0, m ≥ 0, B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w) and μ(B̄_s(z)) ≤ ofReal(m), then ∫⁻_{B̄_s(z)} ‖H‖ₑ^q dμ ≤ ofReal(m^{1-q/p} · t^{q(n-p)/p}) · K(w, t)^q, where K(w, t)^q is the real power in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p q : ℝ) (z w : Amb n ℓ) (s t m : ℝ), 0 < q → q ≤ p → 0 < t → 0 ≤ m → closedBall z s ⊆ closedBall w t → V.weight (closedBall z s) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal m → ∫⁻ x in closedBall z s, ‖H x‖ₑ ^ q ∂V.weight ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (m ^ (1 - q / p) * t ^ (q * (n - p) / p)) * V.scaledLpNorm H p w t ^ q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- μ := V.weight.
- I := ∫⁻_{B̄_t(w)} ‖H‖ₑ^p dμ ∈ [0, ∞].
- Unfolding RectifiableVarifold.scaledLpNorm gives K(w, t) = (ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I)^{1/p}.
- a := q/p and b := 1 - q/p. n stands for (n : ℝ).
- Real powers of nonnegative reals are Real.rpow; powers in [0, ∞] are ENNReal.rpow.

1. Exponents. From p ≥ q > 0: p > 0, a > 0 (div_pos) and a ≤ 1 (div_le_one), so b ≥ 0.

2. Hoelder. Apply the sibling theorem tdo_slb_setLIntegral_rpow_le_holder with X := Amb n ℓ (its Borel measurable-space instance), μ := V.weight, B := B̄_s(z), g := (x ↦ ‖H x‖ₑ), and the given p, q (0 < q and q ≤ p). It gives
   ∫⁻_{B̄_s(z)} ‖H‖ₑ^q dμ ≤ (∫⁻_{B̄_s(z)} ‖H‖ₑ^p dμ)^a · μ(B̄_s(z))^b.

3. Domain and mass.
   - lintegral_mono_set with B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w) gives ∫⁻_{B̄_s(z)} ‖H‖ₑ^p dμ ≤ I.
   - By hypothesis μ(B̄_s(z)) ≤ ofReal(m).
   - Since a, b ≥ 0, ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow on both factors and mul_le_mul' give
     ∫⁻_{B̄_s(z)} ‖H‖ₑ^q dμ ≤ I^a · ofReal(m)^b.

4. ofReal(m)^b = ofReal(m^b) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg, with m ≥ 0 and b ≥ 0).

5. Key identity: I^a = ofReal(t^{q(n-p)/p}) · K(w, t)^q.
   - First, K(w, t)^q = ((ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I)^{1/p})^q = (ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I)^{(1/p)·q} (ENNReal.rpow_mul).
   - (1/p)·q = a (one_div_mul_eq_div), and ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_nonneg (a ≥ 0) gives (ofReal(t^{p-n}) · I)^a = ofReal(t^{p-n})^a · I^a.
   - Next, ofReal(t^{p-n})^a = ofReal((t^{p-n})^a) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg, t^{p-n} ≥ 0) = ofReal(t^{(p-n)·a}) (Real.rpow_mul, t ≥ 0).
   - Hence ofReal(t^{q(n-p)/p}) · K(w, t)^q = (ofReal(t^{q(n-p)/p}) · ofReal(t^{(p-n)·a})) · I^a.
   - The bracket equals ofReal(t^{q(n-p)/p} · t^{(p-n)·a}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, t^{q(n-p)/p} ≥ 0), which is ofReal(t^{q(n-p)/p + (p-n)(q/p)}) (Real.rpow_add, t > 0).
